title: wassname-ml-bench
text: Twelve hard machine learning research problems from wassname’s own work, none of them in any training set, each scored against his own answer. A score of 1.00 means the model matched his answer. The questions stay private, so this page shows the scores and the domains, and nothing that would let a model be trained on them.

Table: score: fraction of wassname’s own answer, so 2.00 would be twice as good as his, according to the judge. Negative means the answer fell into the traps the question sets, which cost more than the rubric points it earned: it did the wrong thing, rather than nothing. $/run: what one pass of all 12 questions costs in this model’s own tokens, judge excluded. ktok: thousands of tokens generated, reasoning included. pts/Mtok: score per million tokens, so a model that thinks its way to the same score ranks lower. answered: the model’s own answers, and below 12 the score is blank, because a mean over fewer questions is not comparable, unless a fallback model fills the refused questions, which the row name and an italic cell say. *: the model refused the question or returned nothing gradable, see Blank cells. Judge spread: the same answers graded by a second judge move a model’s score by 0.04 on average and 0.09 at worst (11 models at v93, deepseek-v4-pro-0813 against gpt-5.6-luna, scripts/scratch/judge_variance.py). Two models inside 0.04 of each other are not separated by this bench. Best in bold, weak arm and calibration arms in italic. v94.
Answered fewer than 12 questions, so their aggregate columns are blank and they are off the chart. Re-run them: anthropic/claude-fable-5 9/12, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (skill:ml-debug) 11/12, moonshotai/kimi-k3 2/12, openai/gpt-5.6-luna 5/12, openai/gpt-5.6-sol 10/12
